node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equal parts of a whole
node.description: Partition one whole into equal-sized parts before naming fractional parts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equal parts of a collection
node.description: Partition a collection into equal groups to represent fractional parts of a set.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit fraction area models
node.description: Represent one equal part of a whole using area models.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit fraction notation
node.description: Read and write unit fractions using numerator, denominator and fraction bar notation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit fractions on number line
node.description: Locate unit fractions between 0 and 1 on a number line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit fraction size
node.description: Reason that unit fractions get smaller as the denominator names more equal parts of the same whole.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Non unit fraction area models
node.description: Represent several equal parts of a whole using area models.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Non unit fractions on number line
node.description: Locate non-unit fractions between whole numbers on a number line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Numerator counts parts
node.description: Interpret the numerator as the number of equal parts being counted.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator names unit size
node.description: Interpret the denominator as the number of equal parts in one whole and therefore the size of each part.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare fractions same denominator
node.description: Compare fractions with the same denominator by comparing the number of equal parts counted.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare fractions same numerator
node.description: Compare fractions with the same numerator by reasoning about the size of the equal parts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent fraction area models
node.description: Use partitioned area models to show different fractions with the same value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent fractions on number lines
node.description: Use number lines to show fractions that occupy the same point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent fraction scaling
node.description: Create equivalent fractions by scaling numerator and denominator by the same nonzero whole number.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Simplify fractions
node.description: Rename a fraction using smaller numerator and denominator while preserving its value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Whole is split into equal parts
node.description: Fractional parts must be equal-sized parts of the same whole.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit fraction is one equal part
node.description: A unit fraction names one equal part of a whole or collection.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator names the unit
node.description: The denominator names how many equal parts make one whole.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Numerator counts fraction units
node.description: The numerator counts how many fractional units are being considered.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same whole is required
node.description: Fractions can be compared or combined meaningfully only when they refer to the same-sized whole or consistent unit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Fractions can name points
node.description: Fractions can locate quantities as points on a number line, not only shaded regions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Larger denominator means smaller unit
node.description: For the same whole, a larger denominator in a unit fraction means smaller equal parts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent fractions name same quantity
node.description: Equivalent fractions use different numbers to name the same quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale numerator and denominator together
node.description: Multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number preserves fraction value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Simplifying preserves value
node.description: Simplifying changes the notation but not the quantity represented by the fraction.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unequal parts are acceptable fractions
node.description: Learner names parts as fractions even when the whole has not been partitioned into equal parts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Denominator counts shaded parts
node.description: Learner treats the denominator as the number of selected or shaded parts rather than total equal parts in the whole.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Larger denominator means larger fraction
node.description: Learner applies whole-number comparison to denominators and thinks larger denominators always mean larger fractions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare numerator and denominator separately
node.description: Learner compares numerators and denominators independently rather than comparing represented quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equivalent fractions change quantity
node.description: Learner treats an equivalent fraction as a different amount because the numerator and denominator changed.

edge.rationale: Unit-fraction work directly practises recognising one equal part of a whole.
Unit fractions can refer to one equal part of a collection as well as one whole.
Area models are a central representation for unit fractions.
Reading and writing unit-fraction notation is core unit-fraction practice.
Number lines show unit fractions as distances and positions from zero.
Reasoning about the size of one equal part is central to unit fractions.
Area models directly practise representing several equal parts.
Number lines support interpreting non-unit fractions as quantities and positions.
Non-unit fractions require counting several fractional units.
Interpreting the denominator as unit size is central to non-unit fractions.
Comparing same-denominator fractions practises counting equal-sized fractional units.
Comparing same-numerator fractions applies reasoning about unit-fraction size.
Area models directly show different partitions preserving the same quantity.
Number lines directly show equivalent fractions at the same point.
Scaling numerator and denominator together is a direct method for generating equivalent fractions.
Simplifying fractions is renaming a fraction using an equivalent form.
Partitioning a whole into fractional parts depends on understanding a collection or whole as a countable total of parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies parts without preserving the whole as the reference quantity.

edge.rationale: Fractions of collections require forming equal groups from a set.
edge.failure_signal: Learner partitions a collection into unequal groups but names them as equal fractional parts.

edge.rationale: A unit-fraction area model requires partitioning the whole into equal parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner shades one part without checking whether all parts are equal-sized.

edge.rationale: Notation for a unit fraction should connect to one equal part of a represented whole.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads 1/4 as two whole numbers rather than one of four equal parts.

edge.rationale: Placing unit fractions on a number line requires interpreting the notation as a fractional distance.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places 1/4 at 4 or treats denominator as a whole-number position.

edge.rationale: Reasoning about unit-fraction size depends on interpreting the denominator as equal parts of one whole.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks 1/8 is larger than 1/4 because 8 is larger than 4.

edge.rationale: Representing several equal parts depends on understanding one fractional unit first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts shaded regions without identifying the size of each unit part.

edge.rationale: The numerator counts how many fractional units are represented in a non-unit fraction model.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain why 3/4 has numerator 3 in a four-part whole with three selected parts.

edge.rationale: Understanding denominator as unit size builds on unit-fraction size reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the denominator only as a count, not as naming the size of each unit part.

edge.rationale: Locating non-unit fractions on a number line requires counting fractional units from zero.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places 3/4 at 3 or 4 rather than three fourth-units from zero.

edge.rationale: With the same denominator, comparison depends on counting how many same-sized parts are present.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not recognise that 3/8 is greater than 2/8 because it has one more eighth.

edge.rationale: Same-numerator comparisons depend on reasoning about the size of each fractional unit.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks 3/8 is greater than 3/4 because 8 is greater than 4.

edge.rationale: Equivalent fraction area models require interpreting represented non-unit fractions as quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sees different partitions but cannot compare the represented shaded amount.

edge.rationale: Recognising equivalent points requires locating non-unit fractions on a number line.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places equivalent fractions at different points based only on their numerals.

edge.rationale: Scaling equivalent fractions should build from seeing that repartitioning can preserve quantity.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes numerator and denominator mechanically without preserving value.

edge.rationale: Simplifying is generating an equivalent fraction with smaller numerator and denominator.
edge.failure_signal: Learner divides only numerator or denominator and changes the fraction's value.
